transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I’m here because I know the new owners are out to destroy my name, no matter what anyone says. They are actively trying to ruin my reputation and make sure I can never work in this industry again.

Besides feeling that the new owners are trying to ruin your reputation, have you also been hearing or seeing things other people do not, or have your thoughts or speech felt confused or hard to follow? If so, when did these experiences start?

No, I don't hear or see things that aren't there, but my head feels stuffed with cotton all the time and I can barely read a text or remember what drink I'm making. This mental cloudiness, along with my certainty about them sabotaging me, all started about two months ago after I sank into this dark, drained state.

Since this started, have you been depressed most of the day nearly every day, with things like loss of interest, poor sleep or appetite, low energy, guilt, or thoughts of death? Or have there been times when your mood felt normal while the belief about the owners still stayed just as strong?

Yes, I've been deeply depressed, exhausted, and barely sleeping or eating every single day for the last two months. This belief about the owners sabotaging me only started after I had already sunk into this dark, hopeless state. My mood has never gone back to normal since this began—these thoughts are completely tied to how drained and hopeless I feel.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F23.3, F23.8, F23.9, F22.0], which focused on acute/transient psychotic states and persistent delusional disorder. Based on this conversation, those are now less likely because the suspicious belief began only after a two-month period of pervasive depressive symptoms, remains present only in the context of the ongoing depressed state, and there are no hallucinations or formal thought disorganization. The delusional content appears mood-congruent and secondary to a severe depressive episode rather than a primary psychotic disorder, so the current candidate is [F32.3].

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a 2-month episode of severe depressive symptoms occurring nearly every day, including depressed mood, anhedonic/drained state, insomnia, poor appetite, low energy, hopelessness, and impaired concentration. A persecutory belief about the new owners sabotaging the patient emerged only after the depressive episode began and has remained fully mood-congruent and confined to the depressive period. The patient denies hallucinations and disorganized thought/speech, supporting a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
